summary: The Qwen3.5 split-checkpoint wrapper did not bind AWQ Marlin's qweight, qzeros, or scales parameters, and packed output tensors require checkpoint split widths adjusted by their pack factor. The change binds those parameters and computes packed split widths before delegating each logical shard to the existing merged-linear loader.

tests.what_was_measured: The primary regression showed the AWQ qweight tuple (0, 1, 2) reached the original loader as one unsplit call. Two boundary assertions also failed before implementation because packed split handling was absent. Raw output: reports/j-d98c9ac9e95a/raw/regression-before.txt

10 loader tests passed, covering AWQ qweight binding, pack-factor splits, group scales, nonzero shard selection, Marlin tiles, input-dimension packing, existing FP8 scale broadcasts, and passthrough behavior. Raw output: reports/j-d98c9ac9e95a/raw/unit-suite.txt

On the assigned MI350X gfx950, split widths were [2, 1, 3], unpacked logical int4 values exactly matched an independently generated tensor, and GPU matrix multiplication had maximum absolute difference 0.0. Raw output: reports/j-d98c9ac9e95a/raw/gpu-packed-loader.txt

gpu_execution_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, ROCm 7.2; exact packed-weight reconstruction and GPU matmul reference comparison are recorded in reports/j-d98c9ac9e95a/raw/gpu-packed-loader.txt
remaining_limitations: QuantTrio/Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ weights were not present in the prepared runtime, so the reported full-model generation degeneration was not reproduced before or after the candidate correction.
The assigned GPU is AMD gfx950, while the report used CUDA sm_120; the AWQ Marlin serving kernel and architecture-specific generation path were therefore not qualified here.

No comparison against vLLM model tensors or semantic output was possible without the checkpoint. The evidence qualifies the defective SGLang weight-loading contract and its correction, not end-to-end model accuracy.
